title: Establishment of a Novel in Vivo Rabbit Model for Hypothermic Machine Perfusion
protocol: Select two male rabbits (body weight 3.2-3.8 kg) each time.
Remove bunk feeders from selected rabbits 36-48 hours before the operation.
Ensure that selected rabbits are fasted for 36 to 48 hours but have access to sufficient water.
Sterilize surgical instruments under high heat and pressure.
Place sterilized instruments on a tray covered with disposable sterile towels prior to surgery.
Fix heating panels and small animal electrotome in place before the operation.
Turn on air conditioning to maintain the operating room at 25°C/50-70% RH.
Switch on shadowless surgical operating lamp.
Anesthetize male rabbits by injecting 1% sodium pentobarbital solution (3 ml/kg body weight) into the right ear marginal vein through a 20 ml syringe.
Weigh anesthetized fasted male rabbits.
Maintain rabbit’s basal body temperature at 38±0.5°C using scalp acupuncture and intravenous injection of 5% glucose solution.
Fix heating plate set at 45.0°C on the operation table.
Place the anesthetized rabbits on the heating plate in a supine position, securing limbs and head to ensure unobstructed breathing.
Prepare the skin between the xiphoid process and symphysis pubis for ventral midline celiotomy.
Prepare sufficient left abdomen and lumbar region skin for surgical procedures.
Prepare left femoral skin for electrode placement.
Paste electrosurgical dispersive plate on prepared left femoral skin area.
Insert rectal temperature probe into the anus after defecation to ensure accurate temperature measurement.
Wash hands according to clinical sterile requirements.
Put on disposable aseptic surgical gowns.
Soak the sterile gauze in povidone iodine.
Disinfect the operation skin completely using the imbricate method.
Repeat the disinfection process two more times.
Drape the abdominal area with a disposable aseptic hole-towel.
Expose the surgical area through the window cut in the middle of the sterile towel.
Connect the electrotome and suction apparatus.
Perform conventional laparotomy by making an abdominal incision from below the xiphoid process to 3-5 cm above the pubic symphysis.
Control bleeding with pressing gauze and electric coagulation if it occurs during skin incision.
Incise the muscle along the linea alba using the electrotome after controlling skin bleeding.
Raise slightly the muscle layer while cutting to protect abdominal viscera from injury.
Use electric coagulation or suture method for hemostasis in case of more bleeding in the muscle layer.
Protect the cut edge with a cotton pad and gauze during exploration.
Push the abdominal organs aside gently towards the right side.
Cover exposed abdominal organs with gauze to protect them.
Maintain moisture and temperature using 45.0°C normal saline to prevent intestinal necrosis and dehydration adhesion.
Expose the left kidney carefully by blunt dissection of the renal vein, taking care not to cause injury or tear.
Determine if there is artery malformation or multiple arteries during blunt dissection of renal artery.
Isolate arterial sheath with a length of 1.5-2cm.
Close the ureter using an artery clamp.
Close the renal artery and vein simultaneously.
Start timing from the moment of clipping the vessels.
Observe changes in kidney color and texture, as well as cessation of arterial beating.
Clip for 25min/35min/45min depending on the experimental condition.
Use tissue forceps to close the abdominal cavity incision.
Maintain basal body temperature at 38±0.5°C.
Draw blood from the vein of the left ear.
Carry out blood gas analysis.
Release the tissue forceps 1 min before reaching 25min/35min/45min reperfusion.
Open the abdominal cavity to expose the left kidney.
Release two arterial clips when reaching 25min/35min/45min.
Observe the renal color and texture; ensure the kidney is reddened, softened without petechiae, and has pulsation of artery restored.
Protect the intestinal tract during the procedure.
Clip the incision skin using tissue forceps to close the abdominal cavity.
Maintain the basal body temperature after closing the abdominal cavity.
Release tissue forceps 30 minutes before the 1-hour mark.
Open the abdominal cavity to expose the left kidney, protecting the intestinal tract carefully.
Change the 5% glucose solution to hydroxyethyl starch solution at a rate of 3 drops per second.
Perform a transverse incision parallel to the left renal pedicle, with an incision length of 7-9 cm, forming a "T" shape with the original incision and stop bleeding.
Inject intravenously 0.3 ml heparin (1875 IU) via the right marginal ear vein.
Prepare the renal artery puncture device including venous indwelling needle, infusion set, and cold heparinized citric acid renal protection solution at 4°C.
Isolate the left kidney with surrounding tissues without cutting the ureter or renal pedicle.
Ligate to stop bleeding and prevent blood infiltration into surrounding tissue.
Clip the renal artery and vein simultaneously using arterial clamps.
Clip the ureter with another arterial clamp.
Tie two 3-0 mousse lines around the renal artery for backup.
Pull the line proximal to the heart with the left hand while puncturing the renal artery with the indwelling needle head with the right hand.
After completion of puncture, open the infusion set.
Prick gently the renal vein with the head of venous indwelling needle after the kidney becomes white.
Observe the perfusing speed to prevent indwelling needle slippage or obstruction.
Start countdown for 4 hours.
Ligate the distal end neither too tight nor too loose to prevent slippage.
Ligate the proximal end.
Place the kidney into a bag filled with 4°C citric acid renal preservation solution.
Tighten the renal bag without obstructing the indwelling needle.
Observe the perfusion velocity.
Take out the kidney bag from the left body of rabbit.
Perform in vivo renal preservation in a round plate filled with ice and water mixture.
Suture “T” shaped cut on the skin.
Prepare the drainage tube and LifePort perfusion apparatus.
Move the rabbit into position to pull out the left kidney through a transverse incision.
Place the drainage tube inside without changing streaming velocity.
Suture the transverse skin incision to close the left abdomen, ensuring it does not influence the streaming velocity.
Place the kidney into a sterile plate filled with crushed ice.
Bury the kidney under crushed ice to maintain hypothermia.
Install the lifeport perfusion apparatus for machine perfusion preservation.
Suture the skin of the abdominal median incision after setting up the apparatus.
Restore the abdominal temperature post-surgery.
Monitor the perfusion flow and ensure the pressure is 60mmHg with a flow rate of 15-20ml/min.
Change the hydroxyethyl starch solution to 5% glucose solution at a rate of 5s/drop.
Observe the rabbit's vital signs for 4 hours, ensuring there is plenty of ice in the plate.
Perform a second blood gas analysis after two hours of preservation to check for drainage tube obstruction.
Carry out the third blood gas analysis 20 minutes in advance before heading to 4 hours.
Prepare 50 ml of 4°C Lactated Ringer's solution.
Prepare 5 ml of sodium bicarbonate.
Prepare 2 ml of heparin.
Prepare 2 ml of furosemide.
Prepare 50 ml of heparin sodium chloride.
Prepare 50 ml of 4°C normal saline.
Open midline incision and the left abdominal transverse incision 5 minutes in advance.
Change to hydroxyethyl starch solution I.V. at a rate of 1 s/drop.
Fill 50 ml of 4°C Lactated Ringer's solution in the kidney to rinse away residual citric acid renal preservation solution.
Suture the vein using a 10-0 sized suture needle with prolene.
Remove the indwelling needle.
Suture the artery using a 10-0 sized suture needle with prolene.
Keep moisture and temperature in the intestine during vascular suturing.
Monitor the vital signs of the rabbit.
Carry out leakage test by clipping distal end of renal artery and vein.
Open two artery clamps to determine bleeding and stenosis in artery and vein.
Recover renal blood supply.
Give intravenous bolus injection of 0.2 ml heparin via the right marginal ear vein.
Give intravenous bolus injection of 0.5 ml furosemide via the right marginal ear vein.
Inject 5 ml of 5% sodium bicarbonate slowly.
Observe vital signs and kidney status of the rabbit.
Conduct the fourth blood gas analysis.
Close the left abdominal transverse incision carefully layer by layer.
Prepare the fistula immediately.
Determine the fistula position.
Use the purse-string suture.
Make sure the bladder should not be strained to injury.
Give intravenous bolus injection of 0.5 ml furosemide through the marginal ear vein.
Separate the right renal pedicle and make double ligation.
Separate the ureter and make double ligation.
Release the tissues around the kidney, and make ligation for hemostasis.
Cut off the renal pedicle and ureter.
Resect the right kidney and stop bleeding.
Give intravenous bolus injection of 0.5 ml furosemide through the marginal ear vein.
Sort and count the apparatus.
Rinse the abdominal cavity.
Close the abdominal cavity carefully layer by layer.
Replace hydroxyethyl starch with lactated Ringer's solution I.V. at a rate of 5 s/drop.
Loosen the rabbit from the fastening device.
Dry the rabbit with blower to restore body temperature as soon as possible.
Clean up the experimental apparatus and equipment.
Clean the perfusion laboratory.
Disinfect the laboratory with UV for backup.
Monitor the vital signs of the rabbit postoperatively.
Monitor the urine volume of the rabbit postoperatively.
Monitor blood gas analysis of the rabbit for 24 hours postoperatively.
Correct disorders of acid-base balance timely.
Supplement blood volume to contribute to the recovery of left kidney function.
Measure the urine volume 24 hours after operation.
Collect the rabbit’s blood into a tube with anticoagulant.
Centrifuge the collected blood for 5 minutes at 2000 rpm to obtain plasma.
Test the plasma for BUN and creatinine using an automatic biochemical analyzer.
Collect another blood sample in a tube without anticoagulant.
Centrifuge this blood sample for 5 minutes at 2000 rpm to obtain serum.
Test the serum content of TNF-α and IL-6 with ELISA kits.
Collect tissue samples to detect cell apoptosis using TUNEL assay.
